dataset.name: Leaf mass per area, by age, Feb2017, PA-SLZ: Panama
description: This data package contains the leaf mass per area (LMA) data of leaves sampled for gas exchange measurements from the Bosque Protector San Lorenzo (PA-SLZ) NGEE Tropics site in Panama during February of 2017. Sunlit canopy leaves of the Apeiba membranacea, Guatteria dumetorum, Miconia borealis, Terminalia amazonia, Virola multiflora, and Vochysia ferruginea species were collected before dawn. Included in the zip file attached are two Excel metadata files and the LMA data file "2017_SLZ_LMA_ByAgeV2." The data has also been included in CSV format, "Panama2017_LMA.csv." Also included is a PDF with leaf sampling protocol. This data was collected as part of the 2017 Brookhaven National Lab and Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute leaf traits by age campaign. Related datasets include further sample details, leaf water potential, sap flow, leaf gas exchange, leaf spectra and leaf chemistry.
This dataset was originally published on the NGEE Tropics Archive and is being mirrored on ESS-DIVE for long-term archival

Acknowledgement: This research was supported as part of NGEE-Tropics, funded by the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Biological and Environmental Research under contract no. DE-SC0012704.

spatialCoverage.description: Site Name: Bosque Protector San Lorenzo (Fort Sherman). Site ID: PA-SLZ. Located in Panama. Established in 1997, the FTS canopy crane is located approximately 11km South West from the city of Colon, in the middle theParque Natural San Lorenzo (formerly known as FortSherman) and is surrounded by 300-year old, low-landtropical rainforest. The crane is 52 meters tall with aradius of 54 meters, and can reach approximately 240species of trees and lianas. (Paton 2015 FTS Met report) For more information on this site, visit: http://biogeodb.stri.si.edu/physical_monitoring/research/sherman,http://www.stri.si.edu/english/research/facilities/terrestrial/cranes/cranes_and_sites.php Site contact(s): (Argelis Ruiz <ruiza@si.edu>)
